name: Isaac
overview: Isaac is a male biblical figure uniquely identified as the son of Abraham and Sarah, marking him as a central figure in God's covenant promises. His life is foundational in the unfolding of God's plan through the patriarchal line. No additional tribal affiliation or notes are specified.
namesAndTitles: Isaac's name, given by God, means 'he laughs,' reflecting the joy and surprise surrounding his birth as foretold by God. This meaning underscores the miraculous nature of Isaac's arrival to his elderly parents.
familyAndRelationships: Isaac is explicitly recorded as the son of Abram (Abraham) and Sarai (Sarah). He is also the father of Esau and Jacob, his twin sons, continuing the covenant lineage. These family connections are central to his role in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Isaac represents the fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham and Sarah, born in their old age as a sign of God's faithfulness. His near-sacrifice by Abraham demonstrates profound faith and prefigures Christ's obedience in sacrifice. Through Isaac, the covenant blessings are preserved and extended, making him a pivotal figure in biblical history.
